evidence: bp-node.lisp:987-1079: fnn-bpnc-accept-loop runs one session to completion, and forwarding, outboxes, receipts, expiry and rotation run only after `(fnn-tcl-session ...)` returns (1060-1077). During the session only *fnn-tcl-progress* runs dispatch-pending (1013-1028). The comment at 1008-1012 concedes that "The forwarding, outbox and receipt sends ... still run between sessions". fnn-tcl-session has no session-duration bound: tcpcl.lisp:499-553 loops while the peer sends keepalives.
fix: Bound each passive session's wall time and work at the host, with ACL2 deciding the bound, and terminate gracefully at the bound. Or run the between-session passes from the same quiet-timeout hook that PKT-873 added for dispatch.
reviewer: bp-node.lisp:973-987 and bp-control.lisp:192-207 run one session to completion before the next poll, which is deliberate (spec 9.1). fnn-tcl-session (tcpcl.lisp:499-553) has no bound on session duration: it loops while the peer sends input or keepalives. Admission is decided per transfer in fnn-bp-deliver-node, not at SESS_INIT (comment at bp-node.lisp:1033-1039), so even an unadmitted peer can complete SESS_INIT and then hold the session. *fnn-tcl-progress* runs only on a read timeout after acknowledged custody (tcpcl.lisp:517-521), and even then only dispatch-pending. Forwarding, outboxes, receipts, expiry (delete-expired) and rotation (bp-node.lisp:1056-1077) never run while the session lasts. The control pump still runs through fnn-bpnc-wait-input.
scenario: Any admitted or unadmitted peer completes SESS_INIT and then only sends KEEPALIVE every 10 s. The node never returns to its accept loop. Other neighbours' connections pile up in the backlog-4 queue and are refused, held rows are never forwarded, owed receipts are never queued or sent, expiry (kind 10) and serve rotation never run, all for as long as the peer likes.
title: Serialized bp-node loop: one peer holding a keepalive session starves every other listener, forwarding and receipts
